requirements.quote: [MQTT-1.5.3-1]	The character data in a UTF-8 encoded string MUST be well-formed UTF-8 as defined by the Unicode specification [Unicode] and restated in RFC 3629 [RFC3629].
requirements.condition: When producing or accepting character data in an MQTT UTF-8 encoded string.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure the character data is well-formed UTF-8 under Unicode and RFC 3629.
requirements.why_checkable: Malformed UTF-8 byte sequences can be supplied to a validator or packet parser.

requirements.quote: In particular this data MUST NOT include encodings of code points between U+D800 and U+DFFF.
requirements.condition: When encoding character data in an MQTT UTF-8 string.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include encodings of code points U+D800 through U+DFFF inclusive.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary and interior surrogate code points can be tested.

requirements.quote: If a Server or Client receives a Control Packet containing ill-formed UTF-8 it MUST close the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: When a Server or Client receives a Control Packet containing ill-formed UTF-8.
requirements.required_behavior: Close the Network Connection.
requirements.error_behavior: Terminate the connection rather than continue processing it.
requirements.why_checkable: An ill-formed packet can be injected and connection closure observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-1.5.3-2]	A UTF-8 encoded string MUST NOT include an encoding of the null character U+0000.
requirements.condition: When producing or validating an MQTT UTF-8 encoded string.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include an encoding of U+0000.
requirements.why_checkable: The UTF-8 bytes for U+0000 can be supplied and checked for rejection.

requirements.quote: If a receiver (Server or Client) receives a Control Packet containing U+0000 it MUST close the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: When a Server or Client receives a Control Packet containing U+0000.
requirements.required_behavior: Close the Network Connection.
requirements.error_behavior: Terminate the connection rather than continue processing it.
requirements.why_checkable: A packet containing U+0000 can be injected and connection closure observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-1.5.3-3]	A UTF-8 encoded sequence 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF is always to be interpreted to mean U+FEFF ("ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE") wherever it appears in a string and MUST NOT be skipped over or stripped off by a packet receiver.
requirements.condition: Whenever byte sequence 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF appears in an MQTT UTF-8 encoded string.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret it as U+FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE.
requirements.why_checkable: The sequence can be placed at multiple string positions and decoded output inspected.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-1.5.3-3]	A UTF-8 encoded sequence 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF is always to be interpreted to mean U+FEFF ("ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE") wherever it appears in a string and MUST NOT be skipped over or stripped off by a packet receiver.
requirements.condition: When a packet receiver encounters 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF in an MQTT UTF-8 string.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Skip over the sequence.
requirements.why_checkable: Decoded character positions can reveal whether the sequence was skipped.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-1.5.3-3]	A UTF-8 encoded sequence 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF is always to be interpreted to mean U+FEFF ("ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE") wherever it appears in a string and MUST NOT be skipped over or stripped off by a packet receiver.
requirements.condition: When a packet receiver encounters 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF in an MQTT UTF-8 string.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Strip the sequence from the string.
requirements.why_checkable: The resulting string can be inspected for the retained U+FEFF character.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.2.2-1]	Where a flag bit is marked as “Reserved” in Table 2.2 - Flag Bits, it is reserved for future use and MUST be set to the value listed in that table.
requirements.condition: When encoding a flag bit marked Reserved in Table 2.2.
requirements.required_behavior: Set it to the value listed in Table 2.2.
requirements.why_checkable: The referenced table values are absent from this chunk, so the expected value for each bit cannot be derived from this evidence alone.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.2.2-2]	If invalid flags are received, the receiver MUST close the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: When a receiver receives invalid flags.
requirements.required_behavior: Close the Network Connection.
requirements.why_checkable: The chunk does not define the complete invalid-flag value set because Table 2.2 is absent, so standalone test inputs are incomplete.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-1]	SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, and PUBLISH (in cases where QoS > 0) Control Packets MUST contain a non-zero 16-bit Packet Identifier.
requirements.condition: When encoding a SUBSCRIBE Control Packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The SUBSCRIBE variable header can be parsed for field presence.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-1]	SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, and PUBLISH (in cases where QoS > 0) Control Packets MUST contain a non-zero 16-bit Packet Identifier.
requirements.condition: When encoding a SUBSCRIBE Packet Identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode it as a 16-bit field.
requirements.why_checkable: The identifier field width can be measured as two bytes.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-1]	SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, and PUBLISH (in cases where QoS > 0) Control Packets MUST contain a non-zero 16-bit Packet Identifier.
requirements.condition: When encoding a SUBSCRIBE Packet Identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use value zero.
requirements.why_checkable: The identifier can be decoded and compared with zero.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-1]	SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, and PUBLISH (in cases where QoS > 0) Control Packets MUST contain a non-zero 16-bit Packet Identifier.
requirements.condition: When encoding an UNSUBSCRIBE Control Packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The UNSUBSCRIBE variable header can be parsed for field presence.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-1]	SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, and PUBLISH (in cases where QoS > 0) Control Packets MUST contain a non-zero 16-bit Packet Identifier.
requirements.condition: When encoding an UNSUBSCRIBE Packet Identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode it as a 16-bit field.
requirements.why_checkable: The identifier field width can be measured as two bytes.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-1]	SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, and PUBLISH (in cases where QoS > 0) Control Packets MUST contain a non-zero 16-bit Packet Identifier.
requirements.condition: When encoding an UNSUBSCRIBE Packet Identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use value zero.
requirements.why_checkable: The identifier can be decoded and compared with zero.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-1]	SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, and PUBLISH (in cases where QoS > 0) Control Packets MUST contain a non-zero 16-bit Packet Identifier.
requirements.condition: When encoding a PUBLISH Control Packet with QoS greater than 0.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The PUBLISH variable header can be parsed for field presence.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-1]	SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, and PUBLISH (in cases where QoS > 0) Control Packets MUST contain a non-zero 16-bit Packet Identifier.
requirements.condition: When encoding a Packet Identifier for a PUBLISH with QoS greater than 0.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode it as a 16-bit field.
requirements.why_checkable: The identifier field width can be measured as two bytes.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-1]	SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, and PUBLISH (in cases where QoS > 0) Control Packets MUST contain a non-zero 16-bit Packet Identifier.
requirements.condition: When encoding a Packet Identifier for a PUBLISH with QoS greater than 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use value zero.
requirements.why_checkable: The identifier can be decoded and compared with zero.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-2]	Each time a Client sends a new packet of one of these types it MUST assign it a currently unused Packet Identifier.
requirements.condition: Each time a Client sends a new SUBSCRIBE packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Assign a currently unused Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: Outstanding identifiers can be compared with the new SUBSCRIBE identifier.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-2]	Each time a Client sends a new packet of one of these types it MUST assign it a currently unused Packet Identifier.
requirements.condition: Each time a Client sends a new UNSUBSCRIBE packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Assign a currently unused Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: Outstanding identifiers can be compared with the new UNSUBSCRIBE identifier.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-2]	Each time a Client sends a new packet of one of these types it MUST assign it a currently unused Packet Identifier.
requirements.condition: Each time a Client sends a new PUBLISH packet with QoS greater than 0.
requirements.required_behavior: Assign a currently unused Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: Outstanding identifiers can be compared with the new PUBLISH identifier.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-3]	If a Client re-sends a particular Control Packet, then it MUST use the same Packet Identifier in subsequent re-sends of that packet.
requirements.condition: When a Client re-sends a particular SUBSCRIBE packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the original SUBSCRIBE Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: Original and retransmitted identifiers can be compared.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-3]	If a Client re-sends a particular Control Packet, then it MUST use the same Packet Identifier in subsequent re-sends of that packet.
requirements.condition: When a Client re-sends a particular UNSUBSCRIBE packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the original UNSUBSCRIBE Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: Original and retransmitted identifiers can be compared.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-3]	If a Client re-sends a particular Control Packet, then it MUST use the same Packet Identifier in subsequent re-sends of that packet.
requirements.condition: When a Client re-sends a particular PUBLISH packet with QoS greater than 0.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the original PUBLISH Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: Original and retransmitted identifiers can be compared.

requirements.quote:
The Packet Identifier becomes available for reuse after the Client has processed the corresponding acknowledgement packet.
In the case of a QoS 1 PUBLISH this is the corresponding PUBACK; in the case of QO2 it is PUBCOMP.
For SUBSCRIBE or UNSUBSCRIBE it is the corresponding SUBACK or UNSUBACK.
requirements.condition: While a Client's QoS 1 PUBLISH awaits its corresponding PUBACK.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep its Packet Identifier unavailable for reuse until PUBACK processing completes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reuse the identifier before processing the PUBACK.
requirements.why_checkable: Identifier allocation can be observed before and after PUBACK processing.

requirements.quote:
The Packet Identifier becomes available for reuse after the Client has processed the corresponding acknowledgement packet.
In the case of a QoS 1 PUBLISH this is the corresponding PUBACK; in the case of QO2 it is PUBCOMP.
For SUBSCRIBE or UNSUBSCRIBE it is the corresponding SUBACK or UNSUBACK.
requirements.condition: While a Client's QoS 2 PUBLISH awaits its corresponding PUBCOMP.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep its Packet Identifier unavailable for reuse until PUBCOMP processing completes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reuse the identifier before processing the PUBCOMP.
requirements.why_checkable: Identifier allocation can be observed before and after PUBCOMP processing.

requirements.quote:
The Packet Identifier becomes available for reuse after the Client has processed the corresponding acknowledgement packet.
In the case of a QoS 1 PUBLISH this is the corresponding PUBACK; in the case of QO2 it is PUBCOMP.
For SUBSCRIBE or UNSUBSCRIBE it is the corresponding SUBACK or UNSUBACK.
requirements.condition: While a Client's SUBSCRIBE awaits its corresponding SUBACK.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep its Packet Identifier unavailable for reuse until SUBACK processing completes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reuse the identifier before processing the SUBACK.
requirements.why_checkable: Identifier allocation can be observed before and after SUBACK processing.

requirements.quote:
The Packet Identifier becomes available for reuse after the Client has processed the corresponding acknowledgement packet.
In the case of a QoS 1 PUBLISH this is the corresponding PUBACK; in the case of QO2 it is PUBCOMP.
For SUBSCRIBE or UNSUBSCRIBE it is the corresponding SUBACK or UNSUBACK.
requirements.condition: While a Client's UNSUBSCRIBE awaits its corresponding UNSUBACK.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep its Packet Identifier unavailable for reuse until UNSUBACK processing completes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reuse the identifier before processing the UNSUBACK.
requirements.why_checkable: Identifier allocation can be observed before and after UNSUBACK processing.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-4]	The same conditions [MQTT-2.3.1-3] apply to a Server when it sends a PUBLISH with QoS >0.
requirements.condition: When a Server re-sends a PUBLISH with QoS greater than 0.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the original PUBLISH Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: Original and retransmitted Server PUBLISH identifiers can be compared.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-4]	The same conditions [MQTT-2.3.1-3] apply to a Server when it sends a PUBLISH with QoS >0.
requirements.condition: While a Server's QoS 1 PUBLISH awaits its corresponding PUBACK.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep its Packet Identifier unavailable for reuse until PUBACK processing completes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reuse the identifier before processing the PUBACK.
requirements.why_checkable: Server identifier allocation can be observed around PUBACK processing.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-4]	The same conditions [MQTT-2.3.1-3] apply to a Server when it sends a PUBLISH with QoS >0.
requirements.condition: While a Server's QoS 2 PUBLISH awaits its corresponding PUBCOMP.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep its Packet Identifier unavailable for reuse until PUBCOMP processing completes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reuse the identifier before processing the PUBCOMP.
requirements.why_checkable: Server identifier allocation can be observed around PUBCOMP processing.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-5]	A PUBLISH Packet MUST NOT contain a Packet Identifier if its QoS value is set to 0.
requirements.condition: When a PUBLISH Packet has QoS 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include a Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The QoS 0 PUBLISH variable header can be parsed for identifier absence.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-6]	A PUBACK, PUBREC or PUBREL Packet MUST contain the same Packet Identifier as the PUBLISH Packet that was originally sent.
requirements.condition: When sending a PUBACK corresponding to an original PUBLISH.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the original PUBLISH Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The identifiers in the PUBLISH/PUBACK exchange can be compared.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-6]	A PUBACK, PUBREC or PUBREL Packet MUST contain the same Packet Identifier as the PUBLISH Packet that was originally sent.
requirements.condition: When sending a PUBREC corresponding to an original PUBLISH.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the original PUBLISH Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The identifiers in the PUBLISH/PUBREC exchange can be compared.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-2.3.1-6]	A PUBACK, PUBREC or PUBREL Packet MUST contain the same Packet Identifier as the PUBLISH Packet that was originally sent.
requirements.condition: When sending a PUBREL corresponding to an original PUBLISH.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the original PUBLISH Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The identifiers in the PUBLISH/PUBREL exchange can be compared.

requirements.quote: Similarly to [MQTT-2.3.1-6], SUBACK and UNSUBACK MUST contain the Packet Identifier that was used in the corresponding SUBSCRIBE and UNSUBSCRIBE Packet respectively.
requirements.condition: When sending a SUBACK for a corresponding SUBSCRIBE.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the SUBSCRIBE Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The identifiers in the SUBSCRIBE/SUBACK exchange can be compared.

requirements.quote: Similarly to [MQTT-2.3.1-6], SUBACK and UNSUBACK MUST contain the Packet Identifier that was used in the corresponding SUBSCRIBE and UNSUBSCRIBE Packet respectively.
requirements.condition: When sending an UNSUBACK for a corresponding UNSUBSCRIBE.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the UNSUBSCRIBE Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The identifiers in the UNSUBSCRIBE/UNSUBACK exchange can be compared.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.0-1]	After a Network Connection is established by a Client to a Server, the first Packet sent from the Client to the Server MUST be a CONNECT Packet.
requirements.condition: After a Client establishes a new Network Connection to a Server.
requirements.required_behavior: Send CONNECT as the first Client-to-Server packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The first packet on a new connection can be captured and classified.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.0-2]	The Server MUST process a second CONNECT Packet sent from a Client as a protocol violation and disconnect the Client.
requirements.condition: When a Server receives a second CONNECT on the same Network Connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Process it as a protocol violation.
requirements.error_behavior: Classify the second CONNECT as a protocol violation.
requirements.why_checkable: A second CONNECT can be injected and the error path observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.0-2]	The Server MUST process a second CONNECT Packet sent from a Client as a protocol violation and disconnect the Client.
requirements.condition: When a Server receives a second CONNECT on the same Network Connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Disconnect the Client.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection closure can be observed independently from error classification.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-1]	If the protocol name is incorrect the Server MAY disconnect the Client, or it MAY continue processing the CONNECT packet in accordance with some other specification.
requirements.condition: When a Server receives a CONNECT with an incorrect protocol name.
requirements.required_behavior: Either disconnect or continue only under another specification.
requirements.why_checkable: Both actions are optional alternatives and the sentence does not require one deterministic outcome.

requirements.quote: In the latter case, the Server MUST NOT continue to process the CONNECT packet in line with this specification.
requirements.condition: When a Server continues processing an incorrect-protocol-name CONNECT under another specification.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Continue processing that CONNECT as MQTT 3.1.1.
requirements.why_checkable: Protocol-path selection can be observed after supplying an incorrect protocol name.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-2]	The Server MUST respond to the CONNECT Packet with a CONNACK return code 0x01 (unacceptable protocol level) and then disconnect the Client if the Protocol Level is not supported by the Server.
requirements.condition: When the CONNECT Protocol Level is unsupported by the Server.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a CONNACK with return code 0x01 for unacceptable protocol level.
requirements.error_behavior: Report the unsupported level using CONNACK code 0x01.
requirements.why_checkable: An unsupported level can be sent and the exact CONNACK code inspected.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-2]	The Server MUST respond to the CONNECT Packet with a CONNACK return code 0x01 (unacceptable protocol level) and then disconnect the Client if the Protocol Level is not supported by the Server.
requirements.condition: After a Server sends CONNACK return code 0x01 for an unsupported Protocol Level.
requirements.required_behavior: Disconnect the Client after sending the CONNACK.
requirements.error_behavior: Terminate the connection after the rejection response.
requirements.why_checkable: Response transmission and subsequent connection closure can be ordered and observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-3]	The Server MUST validate that the reserved flag in the CONNECT Control Packet is set to zero and disconnect the Client if it is not zero.
requirements.condition: When a Server receives a CONNECT Control Packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Validate that its reserved flag is zero.
requirements.why_checkable: CONNECT packets with both reserved-flag values can be supplied to the validator.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-3]	The Server MUST validate that the reserved flag in the CONNECT Control Packet is set to zero and disconnect the Client if it is not zero.
requirements.condition: When a Server receives a CONNECT whose reserved flag is nonzero.
requirements.required_behavior: Disconnect the Client.
requirements.why_checkable: A nonzero reserved flag can be injected and closure observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-4]	If CleanSession is set to 0, the Server MUST resume communications with the Client based on state from the current Session (as identified by the Client identifier).
requirements.condition: When CleanSession is 0 and a Session exists for the Client identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Resume Client communications using that current Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: Persisted state can be created before reconnecting with the same Client identifier and CleanSession 0.

requirements.quote: If there is no Session associated with the Client identifier the Server MUST create a new Session.
requirements.condition: When CleanSession is 0 but no Session exists for the Client identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Create a new Session.
requirements.why_checkable: A previously unseen Client identifier can connect with CleanSession 0 and Server state inspected.

requirements.quote: The Client and Server MUST store the Session after the Client and Server are disconnected.
requirements.condition: After disconnection of a Session established with CleanSession 0.
requirements.required_behavior: The Client must store its Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: Client state can be inspected or exercised after reconnection.

requirements.quote: The Client and Server MUST store the Session after the Client and Server are disconnected.
requirements.condition: After disconnection of a Session established with CleanSession 0.
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must store its Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: Server state can be inspected or exercised after reconnection.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-5]	After the disconnection of a Session that had CleanSession set to 0, the Server MUST store further QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages that match any subscriptions that the client had at the time of disconnection as part of the Session state.
requirements.condition: After disconnection of a CleanSession 0 Session when a further QoS 1 message matches a Subscription held at disconnection.
requirements.required_behavior: Store that message as part of the Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: A matching QoS 1 message can be published while disconnected and recovered after reconnection.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-5]	After the disconnection of a Session that had CleanSession set to 0, the Server MUST store further QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages that match any subscriptions that the client had at the time of disconnection as part of the Session state.
requirements.condition: After disconnection of a CleanSession 0 Session when a further QoS 2 message matches a Subscription held at disconnection.
requirements.required_behavior: Store that message as part of the Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: A matching QoS 2 message can be published while disconnected and recovered after reconnection.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-6]	If CleanSession is set to 1, the Client and Server MUST discard any previous Session and start a new one.
requirements.condition: When a Client connects with CleanSession 1.
requirements.required_behavior: The Client must discard any previous Session.
requirements.why_checkable: Prior Client Session state can be seeded and checked after the clean connection.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-6]	If CleanSession is set to 1, the Client and Server MUST discard any previous Session and start a new one.
requirements.condition: When a Server accepts a connection with CleanSession 1.
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must discard any previous Session for the Client.
requirements.why_checkable: Prior Server Session state can be seeded and checked after the clean connection.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-6]	If CleanSession is set to 1, the Client and Server MUST discard any previous Session and start a new one.
requirements.condition: When a Client connects with CleanSession 1.
requirements.required_behavior: The Client must start a new Session.
requirements.why_checkable: Creation of new Client Session state can be observed after connection.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-6]	If CleanSession is set to 1, the Client and Server MUST discard any previous Session and start a new one.
requirements.condition: When a Server accepts a connection with CleanSession 1.
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must start a new Session for the Client.
requirements.why_checkable: Creation of new Server Session state can be observed after connection.

requirements.quote: This Session lasts as long as the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: For a Session created with CleanSession 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the Session only for the lifetime of its Network Connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Session state can be inspected before and after connection closure.

requirements.quote: State data associated with this Session MUST NOT be reused in any subsequent Session.
requirements.condition: After a CleanSession 1 Session has ended.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reuse its state data in a subsequent Session.
requirements.why_checkable: Distinct subsequent Sessions can be checked for leaked subscriptions or queued messages.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2.7]	Retained messages do not form part of the Session state in the Server, they MUST NOT be deleted when the Session ends.
requirements.condition: When a Server stores retained messages.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep retained messages outside per-Client Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: Retained state ownership can be inspected independently of Client Sessions.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2.7]	Retained messages do not form part of the Session state in the Server, they MUST NOT be deleted when the Session ends.
requirements.condition: When a Client Session ends while retained messages exist.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Delete retained messages because that Session ended.
requirements.why_checkable: A later matching subscription can verify retained messages survive Session termination.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-8]	If the Will Flag is set to 1 this indicates that, if the Connect request is accepted, a Will Message MUST be stored on the Server and associated with the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: When a Server accepts a CONNECT whose Will Flag is 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Store a Will Message on the Server.
requirements.why_checkable: Will state can be inspected or triggered by abnormal connection closure.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-8]	If the Will Flag is set to 1 this indicates that, if the Connect request is accepted, a Will Message MUST be stored on the Server and associated with the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: When a Server stores a Will Message for an accepted CONNECT with Will Flag 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Associate that Will Message with the accepted Network Connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Two connections with distinct Wills can be closed independently and publication correlation observed.

requirements.quote: The Will Message MUST be published when the Network Connection is subsequently closed unless the Will Message has been deleted by the Server on receipt of a DISCONNECT Packet.
requirements.condition: When a Network Connection with a stored Will subsequently closes without the Server having deleted the Will on receipt of DISCONNECT.
requirements.required_behavior: Publish the Will Message.
requirements.why_checkable: The connection can be closed without DISCONNECT and matching subscribers observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-9]	If the Will Flag is set to 1, the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the Connect Flags will be used by the Server, and the Will Topic and Will Message fields MUST be present in the payload.
requirements.condition: When a Server processes an accepted CONNECT whose Will Flag is 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the Will QoS field from the Connect Flags.
requirements.why_checkable: Published Will delivery QoS can be compared with the CONNECT field.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-9]	If the Will Flag is set to 1, the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the Connect Flags will be used by the Server, and the Will Topic and Will Message fields MUST be present in the payload.
requirements.condition: When a Server processes an accepted CONNECT whose Will Flag is 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the Will Retain field from the Connect Flags.
requirements.why_checkable: Will retained-state behavior can be compared with the CONNECT field.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-9]	If the Will Flag is set to 1, the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the Connect Flags will be used by the Server, and the Will Topic and Will Message fields MUST be present in the payload.
requirements.condition: When encoding a CONNECT whose Will Flag is 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the Will Topic field in the payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECT payload can be parsed for Will Topic presence.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-9]	If the Will Flag is set to 1, the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the Connect Flags will be used by the Server, and the Will Topic and Will Message fields MUST be present in the payload.
requirements.condition: When encoding a CONNECT whose Will Flag is 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the Will Message field in the payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECT payload can be parsed for Will Message presence.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-10]	The Will Message MUST be removed from the stored Session state in the Server once it has been published or the Server has received a DISCONNECT packet from the Client.
requirements.condition: Once a stored Will Message has been published.
requirements.required_behavior: Remove it from Server Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: Subsequent connection events can verify the Will is no longer stored or republished.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-10]	The Will Message MUST be removed from the stored Session state in the Server once it has been published or the Server has received a DISCONNECT packet from the Client.
requirements.condition: Once the Server receives DISCONNECT from the Client associated with a stored Will.
requirements.required_behavior: Remove the Will Message from Server Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: After DISCONNECT, later closure or reconnection can verify that the Will is absent.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-11]	If the Will Flag is set to 0 the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the Connect Flags MUST be set to zero and the Will Topic and Will Message fields MUST NOT be present in the payload.
requirements.condition: When encoding a CONNECT whose Will Flag is 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include the Will Topic field in the payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The payload can be parsed for Will Topic absence.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-11]	If the Will Flag is set to 0 the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the Connect Flags MUST be set to zero and the Will Topic and Will Message fields MUST NOT be present in the payload.
requirements.condition: When encoding a CONNECT whose Will Flag is 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include the Will Message field in the payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The payload can be parsed for Will Message absence.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-12]	If the Will Flag is set to 0, a Will Message MUST NOT be published when this Network Connection ends.
requirements.condition: When a Network Connection established with Will Flag 0 ends.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Publish a Will Message for that connection.
requirements.why_checkable: The connection can be ended and publications monitored.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-13]	If the Will Flag is set to 0, then the Will QoS MUST be set to 0 (0x00).
requirements.condition: When encoding a CONNECT whose Will Flag is 0.
requirements.required_behavior: Set Will QoS to 0 (0x00).
requirements.why_checkable: The Will QoS bits can be decoded and compared with zero.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-14]	If the Will Flag is set to 1, the value of Will QoS can be 0 (0x00), 1 (0x01), or 2 (0x02).
requirements.condition: When encoding a CONNECT whose Will Flag is 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Choose Will QoS from 0, 1, or 2.
requirements.why_checkable: The two-bit Will QoS value can be checked against the three-value allowlist.

requirements.quote: It MUST NOT be 3 (0x03).
requirements.condition: When the Will Flag is 1 and Will QoS is encoded.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use Will QoS value 3 (0x03).
requirements.why_checkable: The reserved two-bit value can be generated and detected.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-15]	If the Will Flag is set to 0, then the Will Retain Flag MUST be set to 0.
requirements.condition: When encoding a CONNECT whose Will Flag is 0.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the Will Retain Flag to 0.
requirements.why_checkable: The Will Retain bit can be decoded and compared with zero.
